header:
Date: 2027-09-14 | Start: 16:30 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lin Zhou (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (VitalWorks Head of ML), Diego Ramos (VitalWorks Eng Mgr), Priya Nair (Localization PM)
summary: Discovery / POC scoping to select open-model shortlist for multilingual extraction + classification POC. Discussed success criteria (quality targets, latency/throughput), workload sizing, evaluation plan and timeline (4 week pilot), and security/VPC constraints. Agreed next steps: customer to provide dataset and traffic shape, Redwood to run bench and share results + security docs.
topics: POC success criteria: accuracy, latency, cost
Workload sizing: QPS, batch sizes, sequence lengths
Model shortlist: tradeoffs between Polyglot-7B, Globetrek-13B, Orion-8B-q4
Multilingual support and domain adaptation (legal/compliance text)
Benchmarks: quality tests, latency SLOs, cost estimates
Security: VPC/private deploy vs hosted, SOC2, KMS
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we really appreciate you carving out time. Quick roll call.
[00:07] Maya: Hi this is Maya.
[00:09] Diego: Diego here.
[00:11] Priya: Priya on from localization.
[00:13] Lin: Lin from Redwood SE.
[00:15] Samir: Cool. Goal for today is to scope the POC — pick a small shortlist of open models to run across your multilingual extractor and classification microservices and agree on success criteria. Any blockers off the top?
[00:28] Maya: The big one is data residency and we might need VPC or private deployment for some datasets. Also we care about Spanish/Portuguese/French and some German. Japanese maybe later.
[00:40] Samir: Understood. We'll cover deployment options — hosted sandbox vs private — and Lin will call out what needs to change for VPC.
[00:47] Diego: Quick context: our traffic shape is spiky — a lot of short documents, avg 150 tokens, 95th percentile 600 tokens, peak ~220 req/s for the pipeline. Latency target is sub 200ms p95 for inline extraction, and cost per 1k tokens we'd like to keep under $0.08 — ballpark.
[01:10] Lin: Thanks, that traffic shape helps. For spiky workloads we typically recommend reserved capacity or burstable Dedicated, but for the POC hosted with autoscaling usually suffices to get comparative numbers. We'll size the bench to simulate 220 rps peaks.
[01:25] Maya: Success criteria from our side — extractor F1 >= 0.88 on our labeled set, classification accuracy >= 90% for prioritized labels, latency p95 < 200ms for extraction, and throughput to sustain 220 rps with < 5s cold-start. Also regression checks for Spanish/Portuguese.
[01:41] Samir: That's great and specific — helps us design the bench. For model shortlist we propose three open candidates with different tradeoffs: Polyglot-7B (smaller, faster, strong multilingual pretraining), Globetrek-13B (bigger, better quality on long-form and low-resource languages), and Orion-8B-q4 (quantized variant tuned for low cost). Any other preferences?
[02:03] Priya: Can you repeat the model names? Polyglot-7B?
[02:06] Lin: Yeah Polyglot-7B, Globetrek-13B, Orion-8B-q4. Note: names are shorthand, we'll include exact repo/model IDs in the follow-up.
[02:18] Diego: From an infra POV if Orion is quantized heavily, does that affect accuracy for legal named entity extraction? Legal domain uses lots of shorthand and specific terms.
[02:28] Lin: Good question. Quantization (Q4) will lower memory and cost but can slightly affect rare token modeling. We'll include domain-adapted fine-tuning step for the top candidate if quality gaps show. Also we can run a lightweight LoRA on Polyglot-7B to see if that closes the gap without heavy infra.
[02:45] Samir: Important to note: the POC's primary goal is model-level comparison on your real data to inform a longer Dedicated deployment decision. So we'll show you per-model latency/cost profiles, and quality metrics broken down by language and label.
[02:58] Maya: Perfect. Timeline? We need results fast — ideally within 3–4 weeks.
[03:03] Samir: We think a 4-week POC is doable: week 0 — onboarding + security review; week 1 — benchmark harness + baseline runs; week 2 — fine-tune/LoRA experiments on top candidates; week 3 — final run, analysis, and recommendations.
[03:18] Diego: That aligns. On security: we need SOC2 report, network flow diagram, and KMS integration details for encryption at rest. Also RBAC for tokens.
[03:28] Lin: We'll share the security pack and a data flow diagram. For VPC private deployment there's a checklist — if you want private we can provision a sandbox VPC or provide an on-prem package but that'll lengthen time by 1–2 weeks.
[03:43] Maya: Sandbox hosted + VPC peering would be ideal for the POC if possible.
[03:48] Samir: We'll propose hosted sandbox with optional VPC peering. For the bench we'll ask you to provide: (1) 1k labeled examples across languages, (2) a traffic distribution CSV, (3) a list of high-priority labels.
[03:59] Priya: We'll prepare the 1k samples but some are under NDA — can we mask PII and still be useful?
[04:06] Lin: Totally fine, anonymized is preferred. Also include edge-case documents and some failure cases.
[04:12] Maya: On evaluation metrics: besides F1 and accuracy we'd like per-language confusion matrices and a recall metric for critical labels.
[04:19] Samir: We'll include those in the eval sheet. We'll also run latency profiling with your token distribution and show token-level cost breakdowns in the console.
[04:28] Diego: Bench harness question: do you run with continuous batching and prefix cache? Our pipeline benefits from prefix caching because many docs share repeated headers.
[04:36] Lin: Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching and continuous batching. For the benchmark we'll test with and without caching to show cost/latency deltas. Also we can simulate persistent sessions to see KV hit rates.
[04:49] Priya: For localization, we care about small-string translation quality as well. Should we include a small translation test?
[04:54] Samir: Yes include translation as a secondary task — we'll score BLEU/chrF for short snippets.
[04:58] Maya: Any red flags on model licensing if we want to move to production later? We prefer permissive licenses.
[05:03] Lin: We'll flag license types in the summary. Polyglot-7B and Globetrek-13B are permissive-ish, Orion q4 variant is community-redistributable, but we'll provide exact license text in the follow-up.
[05:14] Diego: Cost targets — we said <$0.08 per 1k tokens earlier, is that realistic on hosted?
[05:20] Samir: For the POC hosted numbers will vary by model and quantization. We'll provide per-model cost estimates at the token distribution you share. For Dedicated you can usually push unit costs lower via reserved capacity.
[05:29] Maya: Are there any quick performance expectations? Like Polyglot-7B p95 latency?
[05:33] Lin: Rough ballpark on modern infra: Polyglot-7B ~80–150ms p95 (depending on batch), Orion-8B-q4 ~60–120ms but quantization may slightly hurt rare-token quality, Globetrek-13B ~180–300ms p95 for long sequences. We'll measure all these.
[05:49] Priya: Does Redwood provide a way to pin model versions for the POC so we can reproduce runs?
[05:53] Samir: Yes, we give immutable model hashes and versioned endpoints so you can reproduce. We'll include a repeatable pipeline in the repo link.
[05:59] Diego: On instrumentation, can you emit per-request traces and token-level cost?
[06:03] Lin: Yep, token-level cost, latencies, and per-route dashboards will be available. We can also emit traces to your preferred tracing backend.
[06:11] Maya: Ok great. Anything else?
[06:13] Samir: Let's summarize agreed success criteria so we all have the same yardstick. Maya listed F1 >= 0.88, accuracy >= 90%, latency p95 < 200ms for extraction, throughput to handle 220 rps peaks; we add cost per 1k token goal and regression checks for es/pt. Is that accurate?
[06:30] Maya: Yes.
[06:31] Priya: Yes.
[06:33] Samir: Next procedural steps — I'll send the POC SOW and pricing bands, Lin will share the bench harness repo and a small test script. We will provision a hosted sandbox workspace and credentials for the Redwood console.
[06:45] Lin: Also we'll attach a short checklist for VPC peering if you want that enabled.
[06:50] Diego: Good. One last question — if a single model doesn't meet our locale targets, can Redwood support hybrid routing? e.g., route Spanish requests to a larger model and others to a smaller model?
[07:00] Lin: Yes, smart routing is supported — you can route by language, latency, or cost policy. For POC we'll show the single-model comparison first then a hybrid policy if needed.
[07:10] Maya: That would be useful.
[07:12] Samir: Ok wrapping up. We'll target the kickoff week of 2027-09-20. I'll send notes and the security pack after this call. Thanks everyone.
[07:20] Maya: Thanks all.
[07:22] Diego: Thanks.
[07:23] Priya: Bye.
[07:25] Speaker 6: [recording stopped]
